title: Career highlights: the Miles Davis albums and fear of a wax-museum future
summary: Gil says he has not had much of a career. The Miles Davis albums were his favorite.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I want to move on. I was asking you about some places that you had lived that might have stood out in your memory. And I wonder what you would consider some of the highlights of your career? I know you've gotten awards. You've played in very, very famous festivals and concerts.

I haven't really done that much yet you know. I don't feel that I have really had much of a career. It's been very spotty and very occasional and it's hard for me to assess, to asses it as, that's one of the reasons why I wasn't terribly

enthusiastic about having this kind of an interview because I didn't really feel that I wanted to be placed by anybody else or myself in a wax museum future now because I still have my/career in mind, you know.

So to speak of what I've done in the past and highlights, I have to know that there have been highlights somewhere but they don't seem to have been enough of them or a steady enough pursuit in my trade really to talk about it much. But of course naturally the albums I made with Miles Davis was the most fun I had. And the hardest work, but the most fun. And I had fun making my own albums too, I've enjoyed all the albums I've made really.
